themes_detail.label: Curb Collapse Accelerating
themes_detail.summary: Curb condition complaints surged to 6 THIS WEEK, a 220% spike versus the 1.9-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks, signaling rapid deterioration of street infrastructure in Greenwich Village/SoHo.
evidence: 6 curb condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (220% increase, z-score: 4.45)
Curb complaints are high-severity infrastructure signals that can indicate subway undermining, water main pressure, or freeze-thaw damage
Community Board has repeatedly requested catch basin cleaning and street maintenance funding, suggesting chronic underinvestment in street infrastructure
reporting_angles: On-the-ground photo/video tour of worst curb damage in SoHo and Greenwich Village; interview DOT about repair backlog
Investigate whether recent cold snaps or water main work correlates with curb failures; interview DEP and DOT maintenance supervisors

themes_detail.label: Encampment Crisis Intensifies
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints nearly quadrupled LAST WEEK to 52 complaints, a 333% spike versus the 12-complaint weekly baseline over 8 weeks, indicating a sharp deterioration in street homelessness in the district.
evidence: 52 encampment complaints LAST WEEK vs. 12.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (333% increase, z-score: 4.11)
Community Board budgetary requests include 'public health issues' programs, indicating homelessness and street conditions are persistent district concerns
SoHo and Greenwich Village are high-visibility areas with dense retail/hospitality, making encampment issues politically salient
reporting_angles: Interview affected business owners and residents in heavily impacted blocks (Spring St, Bleecker St, Houston St areas); document specific locations
Track NYPD/Sanitation response times to encampment complaints; interview social services agencies about capacity constraints and shelter availability

themes_detail.label: Litter Basket Emergency
themes_detail.summary: Litter basket complaints exploded to 3 LAST WEEK from a near-zero 0.1-complaint weekly average, a 2300% spike (z-score: 8.69, highest in data), indicating potential infrastructure failure or collection service breakdown.
evidence: 3 litter basket complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (2300% increase, z-score: 8.69, highest severity)
Community Board has repeatedly requested increased sanitation trucks and equipment, suggesting Sanitation Department capacity constraints
Litter basket complaints are usually rare, making this spike a statistical anomaly worth investigating for systemic failure
reporting_angles: Interview Sanitation Department about collection schedule changes, equipment failures, or staffing shortfalls in CD 102 last week
Document specific locations where litter baskets are overflowing or malfunctioning; photograph visual conditions

themes_detail.label: Root and Sewer Infrastructure Damage
themes_detail.summary: Root/sewer/sidewalk condition complaints spiked to 4 complaints TWO WEEKS AGO, a 1500% increase versus 0.2 weekly average (z-score: 8.66), indicating subsurface infrastructure stress in Greenwich Village/SoHo.
evidence: 4 root/sewer/sidewalk complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1500% increase, z-score: 8.66)
Combined with curb condition spike THIS WEEK, suggests district-wide pavement/subsurface degradation pattern
Community Board repeatedly requests catch basin cleaning and street tree maintenance, indicating known chronic underground infrastructure issues
reporting_angles: Investigate ConEd, water mains, and subway tunnel infrastructure for recent failures or pressure anomalies; FOIA recent work orders
Interview residents with basement flooding, cracked foundations, or tree damage; correlate with DEP sewer maps and aging infrastructure zones

themes_detail.label: Beach/Pool/Sauna Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Beach/pool/sauna complaints tripled to 3 THIS WEEK from a baseline of 0.2 weekly average, a 1100% spike (z-score: 4.16), potentially indicating a public facility closure, hygiene issue, or operating-hours disruption.
evidence: 3 beach/pool/sauna complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1100% increase, z-score: 4.16)
No public beaches in Greenwich Village/SoHo proper, so complaints likely refer to indoor pools/saunas at YMCA or private facilities
Unusual spike suggests acute facility closure, maintenance issue, or health violation rather than chronic complaint pattern
reporting_angles: Identify which facilities (YMCA, private gyms/saunas) have recent Health Dept. violations or closures; check DOH inspection records
Interview facility operators and users about service disruptions, maintenance work, or safety concerns driving complaints
